ask.text: When you set the look once in the provider, should it control only toggle buttons (on/off state, check mark), or every ZestButton in the app (plain, danger, outline and so on) as well?
ask.why: It decides how many button kinds and states get style settings, and how much existing appearance has to be re-checked so apps already using the library do not change.

options.label: All buttons, with toggle on/off states included (recommended)
options.consequence: One place styles every button kind, size, variant and hover effect, and the toggle's off/on looks too. Biggest scope, but matches 'apply system wide'.

options.label: Toggle buttons only for now
options.consequence: Smaller change: only the on/off look, check mark, sizes and hover for toggles are configurable; other buttons stay as they are today.

options.label: Toggle buttons first, but built so other kinds can be added later
options.consequence: Only toggles are configurable in this release, with a settings shape that other button kinds can join later without breaking anyone.

coverage.note: Developers who install the library and wrap their app in the provider; end users see the result.
Which buttons the provider styling reaches.
A UI library: no records or ownership.
Unknown or invalid style values are ignored safely and never break rendering.
Toggle on/off, hover, disabled, busy states already decided; styling must cover them.
No submissions or shared records in the styling settings.
Settings are one small object; render cost is covered under quality.
Light/dark/system themes, keyboard focus visibility, rem units, no needless re-renders, additive and non-breaking.

assumptions: Invalid or unknown style values are ignored without crashing.
The change is additive: apps that do not use the new styling settings look exactly as they do today.
Quality: works in light, dark and system themes, keeps a visible keyboard focus indicator, uses rem sizes, and does not re-render buttons when the settings object is unchanged.
